content: The text provided is a long list of references, citations, and affiliations related to various research studies, reports, and academic contributions in the field of global health, infectious diseases, and medical research. It includes detailed information about authors, their roles, institutions, and the focus of their work. 1. Xiao S and colleagues conducted recent investigations into artemether, a novel agent for the prevention of schistosomiasis japonica, mansoni, and haematobia. Their findings were published in Acta Tropica in 2002, volume 82, issue 2, pages 175–181. 2. Grace C explored the impact of changing intellectual property laws on the pharmaceutical industry's prospects in India and China, with a focus on access to medicine. This work was documented in a PDF accessed on March 2, 2012. 3. Tanner M, Kitua A, and Degremont AA described the development of health research capacity in Tanzania, transitioning from a Swiss Tropical Institute Field Laboratory to the Ifakara Centre of the Tanzanian National Institute of Medical Research. This was published in Acta Tropica in 1994, volume 57, issues 2–3, pages 153–173. 4. Ofori-Adjei D emphasized the importance of investing in health research for endemic diseases in the Ghana Medical Journal, 2008, volume 42, issue 3, page 95. 5. The WHO Technical Report Series No. 972 (2012) outlined research priorities for helminth infections, as detailed in the technical report of the TDR Disease Reference Group on Helminth Infections. 6. Bonfoh B and colleagues discussed the challenges of conducting research in war zones in an article published in Nature in 2011, volume 474, issue 7353, pages 569–571. 7. Guidelines for research partnerships with developing countries were outlined in a document titled 11 Principles, accessed on March 2, 2012. 8. The Swiss Commission for Research Partnerships with Developing Countries (KFPE) published 12 Principles in 2000, emphasizing ethical and effective collaboration in research. 9. Ofori-Adjei D and Gyapong J provided a developing country perspective on international health research partnerships in a PDF accessed on March 2, 2012. 10. Bethony JM and Loukas A reviewed the current research agenda for schistosomiasis in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases, 2008, volume 2, issue 2, article e207. 11. Young J and Kannemeyer N conducted a study mapping existing initiatives to build research capacity in Southern regions, documented in a main report. 12. Binka F, in an editorial published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in 2005, volume 10, issue 3, pages 207–209, discussed the shift towards true partnerships in North-South research collaborations. 13. The Abuja Declaration on HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and other related infectious diseases was documented in a PDF accessed on March 2, 2012. 14. The Algiers Declaration (June 2008) focused on narrowing the knowledge gap to improve Africa’s health, as detailed in a PDF accessed on May 2, 2012. 15. The Bamako Call to Action on Research for Health emphasized strengthening research for health, development, and equity, as outlined in a PDF accessed on March 2, 2012. 16. The Commission on Health Research for Development highlighted the essential link between health research and equity in development in a publication by Oxford University Press in 1990. 17. The World Bank's Accra Agenda for Action was documented in a PDF. 18. Nuyens Y argued that development cannot occur without research, emphasizing the need for strengthening research capacity. 19. Utzinger J and Keiser J reviewed common drugs for the treatment and control of schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminthiasis in Expert Opinion in Pharmacotherapy, 2004, volume 5, issue 2, pages 263–285. 20. Fürst T, Keiser J, and Utzinger J conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the global burden of human food-borne trematodiasis, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases, 2012, volume 12, issue 3, pages 210–221. 21. Utzinger J proposed a research and development agenda for the control and elimination of human helminthiases in an editorial published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases, 2012, volume 6, issue 4, article e1646. 22. Lustigman S and colleagues outlined a research agenda for helminth diseases of humans, focusing on basic research and enabling technologies to support control and elimination, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases, 2012, volume 6, issue 4, article e1445. 23. McCarthy JS and colleagues emphasized the need for improved diagnostics for helminth disease control and elimination programs in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases, 2012, volume 6, issue 4, article e1601. 24. Osei-Atweneboana MY and colleagues discussed health research and capacity building in disease-endemic countries for helminthiasis control in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases, 2012, volume 6, issue 4, article e1602. 25. Annex 1 of the WHO Technical Report Series No. 972 (2012) detailed the TDR Disease and Thematic Reference Groups, including their host institutions and countries. 26. Annex 2 provided the membership details of the Disease Reference Group on Helminth Infections (DRG4), listing experts, their countries, expertise, and gender. 27. Annex 3 outlined the composition of the TDR Think Tank, including prominent researchers and their affiliations across various global institutions.
